recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not restore the older verification-status-only definition unless Patient Care reopens the post-FHIR-42981 scope of Condition.evidence.
issue_request: FHIR-15610 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request to update the Condition.evidence definition to say it is supporting evidence or manifestations that are the basis of the Condition's verification status, including evidence that confirmed or refuted the condition. Patient Care also decided not to correlate each individual evidence code or reference with Condition.verificationStatus.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-15610-tagged commit was found in the current HL7/fhir history. The requested wording appears in the published R4 and R5 Condition profiles and was present in the current source history before c71dae0dd9384f14d337a2251452dbdac2f6ea14, so the substance of the seed issue had been applied before this reconciliation. FHIR-11026 later reinforced the same refuted-evidence guidance in Condition notes.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Patient Care issues changed the same element: FHIR-32481 converted Condition.evidence to CodeableReference while preserving examples and cumulative-evidence guidance, and FHIR-42981 intentionally broadened the short text and definition beyond verification status to support determining the Condition more generally. FHIR-42981 is already represented on the combined branch by 649da8cc5530b17052aea78ac1a8185f3f8df788.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reinstating the exact FHIR-15610 wording would undo the later FHIR-42981 clarification, while the current authoritative source still preserves confirmed/refuted evidence guidance in the Condition.evidence comment and Condition notes.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Patient Care issue repeated the FHIR-15610 definition and added explicit guidance that evidence of a refutation can be conveyed in Condition.evidence.
